summary: Teton forest lookout from the 1930s program; permanent station 1942, manned 1954, listed as gone with no removal year.

facts.design: ground-type lookout; the 1942 permanent station was assembled at the Jackson Forest Service property, dismantled and hauled to the site by truck
facts.status_note: listed as gone in the Forest Fire Lookout Association inventory; no removal year or reason in the sources

staffing.status: listed among Teton lookouts to be manned within the next week in July 1954

facts.agency: Teton National Forest, administratively consolidated with the Bridger National Forest on July 1, 1973; site now listed under Bridger-Teton National Forest

events.note: permanent station, assembled at the Jackson Forest Service property, dismantled and hauled by truck to the site

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NRHP nomination dates the start of the six-lookout program to the 1930s, while the August 1942 Jackson's Hole Courier item names Baldy's permanent station; the story gives both dates for their own points and does not treat them as contradictory.

sources.title: Huckleberry Mountain Lookout, National Register of Historic Places nomination

notes_for_editor: No removal year, cause or current-site description found in the sources; the Gone status rests on the FFLA inventory alone. A 1941 Jackson Hole Courier item about four new Teton lookout houses does not name Baldy, so it is not used. The NRHP nomination is for Huckleberry Mountain Lookout and mentions Baldy only as one of the six sites. firelookout.com gives the agency as Bridger-Teton. A records check with the Bridger-Teton National Forest would be the next step for a removal date.
